description.narrative: In March 2023, the Government through the Ministry of Labour in consultation with social partners and stakeholders across the skills ecosystem developed the Mauritius’ Skills Mobility Framework to ensure effective skills mobility governance and efficient labour migration management, to enhance employability, labour market responsiveness and entrepreneurship performance through improved skills anticipation (recognition of present skill needs and rapid labour shortages’ projections), skills transfer programmes and skills recognition mechanisms. The framework was based on ILO standards, methodologies and tools related to Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and the mutual recognition of qualifications. With support from the European Union, the ILO supported the country to develop the Mauritius’ Skills Mobility Framework. The ILO also conveyed several consultation meetings and one virtual tripartite validation workshop from January to March 2023 to discuss the draft framework and undertook a technical revision of the final version. The framework was validated based on the ILO and the stakeholders comments.

description.narrative:
The Government in consultation with employers and workers organizations, undertook a rapid skills needs assessment in marine-based renewable energy in Mauritius which intends to identify and measure skills mismatches and anticipate future skills needs. It was undertaken in consideration to the labour market supply and demands in response to marine-based renewable energy technology and environmental changes, including the impact of the COVID-19 by using the ILO ‘Guidelines on rapid assessment of reskilling and upskilling needs in response to the COVID-19 crisis’. The report of the assessment has been validated by stakeholders during a validation workshop on 14 June 2023.
With support from the SDG Funds, the ILO supported the country to undertake a rapid skills needs assessment in marine-based renewable energy in Mauritius and developed a report of the related results by using its methodology and according to its ‘Guidelines on rapid assessment of reskilling and upskilling needs in response to the COVID-19 crisis’. The ILO also conveyed several consultation meetings and one virtual tripartite validation workshop on 14 June 2023 to discuss the draft report and undertook a technical revision of the final version. The report was validated based on the ILO and the stakeholders comments.
